question.problem:
Consider the function $f:R\to {R}^{4},$ defined by 

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 \\ 4 & -5 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x?$
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $f:R\to {R}^{m}$ with respect to a scalar $x$ is the column vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} \\ ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂x}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{m\times 1}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a scalar $x\in R,$ and

- outputs a vector $f(x)\in {R}^{4}$ defined by 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 \\ 4 & -5 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}x+2 \\ 3x \\ 4x-10 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{4}}{∂x}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+2) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(3x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(4x-10) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(6)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{4\times 1}.\end{aligned}
$$
